MetaCONCUR 0.0.0.1
  • Reference

    MetaCONCUR

    An R package for CNV meta-analysis using summary statistics. Includes two steps: 1. Worker step, which takes individual-level data input and generate portable summary statistics for each study; 2. Meta steps, which collects and aligns study-specific summary statistics, then performs meta-analysis to get p-value.

    Installation

    You can install the development version of MetaCONCUR like so:

    # install.packages("devtools")
    devtools::install_github("YuhuanC/MetaCONCUR")

    Examples

    This is a basic example which shows you how to run Worker step and obtain summary statistics for one study:

    library(MetaCONCUR)
# Load example data
data(cnvData)
data(phenoData)
data(covData)
# Run on example data, first 100 individuals
s1_cnv <- cnvData[as.numeric(sub("P", "", cnvData$ID)) >= 1 &
                  as.numeric(sub("P", "", cnvData$ID)) <= 100, ]
s1_pheno <- phenoData[as.numeric(sub("P", "", phenoData$ID)) >= 1 &
                      as.numeric(sub("P", "", phenoData$ID)) <= 100, ]
s1_cov <- covData[as.numeric(sub("P", "", covData$ID)) >= 1 &
                  as.numeric(sub("P", "", covData$ID)) <= 100, ]
cutoff.dup <- 2.3
cutoff.del <- 1.7
formula_bin <- PHEB ~ SEX
# Run Worker to get summary statistics for chromosome 1
s1_SS <- CONCUR_worker(
  cnvData = s1_cnv,
  phenoData = s1_pheno,
  cutoff.dup = cutoff.dup,
  cutoff.del = cutoff.del,
  formula = formula_bin,
  covData = s1_cov,
  phenoType = "bin",
  chr = 1,
  use.big.memory = FALSE,
  save_dir = NULL
 )
#> No save_dir provided, summary statistics not saved for chr1
# Output is a list of summary statistics
names(s1_SS)
#> [1] "chr1"
names(s1_SS$chr1)
#> [1] "grid" "SSA"  "SSB"  "HAHA" "HAHB" "HBHB" "HAX"  "HBX"

    Another example which shows you how to run Meta step for multiple studies and get p-value of association tests:

    library(MetaCONCUR)
# Load example data
data(cnvData)
data(phenoData)
data(covData)
# Run on example data, first 100 individuals for study 1
s1_cnv <- cnvData[as.numeric(sub("P", "", cnvData$ID)) >= 1 &
                  as.numeric(sub("P", "", cnvData$ID)) <= 100, ]
s1_pheno <- phenoData[as.numeric(sub("P", "", phenoData$ID)) >= 1 &
                       as.numeric(sub("P", "", phenoData$ID)) <= 100, ]
s1_cov <- covData[as.numeric(sub("P", "", covData$ID)) >= 1 &
                  as.numeric(sub("P", "", covData$ID)) <= 100, ]
# Run on example data, 101-200 individuals for study 2
s2_cnv <- cnvData[as.numeric(sub("P", "", cnvData$ID)) >= 101 &
                  as.numeric(sub("P", "", cnvData$ID)) <= 200, ]
s2_pheno <- phenoData[as.numeric(sub("P", "", phenoData$ID)) >= 101 &
                      as.numeric(sub("P", "", phenoData$ID)) <= 200, ]
s2_cov <- covData[as.numeric(sub("P", "", covData$ID)) >= 101 &
                  as.numeric(sub("P", "", covData$ID)) <= 200, ]
cutoff.dup <- 2.3
cutoff.del <- 1.7
formula_bin <- PHEB ~ SEX
# Getting summary statistics for study 1,2 chromosome 1
s1_SS <- CONCUR_worker(
  cnvData = s1_cnv,
  phenoData = s1_pheno,
  cutoff.dup = cutoff.dup,
  cutoff.del = cutoff.del,
  formula = formula_bin,
  covData = s1_cov,
  phenoType = "bin",
  chr = 1,
  use.big.memory = FALSE,
  save_dir = NULL
)
#> No save_dir provided, summary statistics not saved for chr1
s2_SS <- CONCUR_worker(
  cnvData = s2_cnv,
  phenoData = s2_pheno,
  cutoff.dup = cutoff.dup,
  cutoff.del = cutoff.del,
  formula = formula_bin,
  covData = s2_cov,
  phenoType = "bin",
  chr = 1,
  use.big.memory = FALSE,
  save_dir = NULL
)
#> No save_dir provided, summary statistics not saved for chr1
# Running Meta with two studies' SS chr1, if SS not exists, load
res_p <- Meta(s1_SS$chr1, s2_SS$chr1)

print(res_p)
#>    davies       liu 
#> 0.7437512 0.7222249

    Here’s another example to load the external study-specific summary statistics and perform meta-analysis using MetaCONCUR:

    load_chr_stats(chr_name = "chr1", save_dir = tmp, use.big.memory = FALSE)

    You’ll still need to render README.Rmd regularly, to keep README.md up-to-date. devtools::build_readme() is handy for this. You could also use GitHub Actions to re-render README.Rmd every time you push. An example workflow can be found here: https://github.com/r-lib/actions/tree/v1/examples.
